goldenPoints: Stranger anxiety appears around 6–9 months; transfer of objects hand-to-hand at about 7 months
Familial short stature: bone age equals chronological age; constitutional delay: bone age is delayed
Chest compressions in a newborn start when the heart rate stays below 60/min despite ventilation
Vitamin K at birth prevents haemorrhagic disease of the newborn
Plan B for some dehydration: ORS 75 mL/kg over 4 hours; zinc for 14 days
ASD gives a fixed, widely split second heart sound; TOF gives a boot-shaped heart
Minimal change disease is the commonest cause of childhood nephrotic syndrome — steroids first
Measles needs vitamin A; diphtheria shows a bleeding pseudomembrane and bull neck
Down syndrome is trisomy 21; cri-du-chat is a 5p deletion with a cat-like cry
Sweat chloride is the gold standard test for cystic fibrosis
intro: Paediatrics contributes 15 questions to every FMGE paper, drawn from a very repeatable pool: milestones with exact ages, neonatal emergencies, dehydration plans, classic syndromes and vaccine-era infections. These 12 topics are built from what the last five years of papers actually asked.

branches.label: Development & Growth
leaves: Social smile 2 months, stranger anxiety 6–9 months
Pincer grasp 9–10 months, walks alone ~12–15 months
Bone age separates familial from constitutional short stature
Laron dwarfism: GH high, IGF-1 low

branches.label: Neonate
leaves: Compressions if heart rate below 60 despite ventilation
Term resuscitation starts with room air
Vitamin K prevents haemorrhagic disease
Meconium should pass within 24–48 hours

branches.label: Surgical Neonate
leaves: TEF: frothy saliva, tube will not pass
Omphalocele has a sac; gastroschisis does not
CHPS: olive mass, non-bilious vomiting
Hirschsprung: biopsy is the gold standard

branches.label: Nutrition
leaves: SAM: MUAC below 11.5 cm or oedema
Rickets: craniotabes, rosary, wide wrists
Acrodermatitis enteropathica = zinc deficiency
Vitamin A treats measles and xerophthalmia

branches.label: Infections
leaves: Measles: Koplik spots, rash behind ears
Diphtheria: pseudomembrane, bull neck
Kawasaki: IVIG plus aspirin
Meningitis in infants: Streptococcus pneumoniae

branches.label: Systems Favourites
leaves: ASD: fixed split S2; TOF: boot-shaped heart
Nephrotic syndrome: minimal change, steroids
Haemophilia A: aPTT up, PT normal

Cri-du-chat: 5p deletion, cat cry

subject: Paediatrics
tagline: Milestones, the newborn, dehydration plans and classic syndromes — a small, very repeatable pool worth 15 questions.

topics.oneLiner: Smile 2, sit 8, stranger anxiety 6–9, transfer 7, pincer 9–10, walk 12–15, tower of six cubes at 2 years.
points: Social smile appears by 2 months; the baby recognises and responds to the mother's face by about 3 months
Head control is achieved by 3–4 months
Sits without support by 7–8 months; sits briefly leaning on hands (tripod) around 6 months
Transfers objects from one hand to the other at about 6–7 months
Stranger anxiety appears around 6–9 months
Mature pincer grasp develops by 9–10 months; waves bye-bye around 9–12 months
Walks alone by 12–15 months; builds a tower of 6 cubes and uses pronouns ('I', 'me') by 2 years
Reflexes present from birth that never disappear: swallowing, gagging and cough
IQ 50–70 is mild intellectual disability; IQ 55 falls in the mild range
topics.title: Developmental Milestones & Reflexes
topics.trap: Stranger anxiety is a 6–9 month milestone — students often place it at 3 months, which is social recognition, not anxiety.

topics.askedAs: familial vs constitutional from bone age
topics.oneLiner: Bone age equal to age = familial; bone age behind = constitutional delay or a systemic cause.
points: Familial short stature: height matches the parents, growth velocity normal, bone age equals chronological age
Constitutional delay: bone age is delayed, puberty is late, final height is usually normal
Upper segment : lower segment ratio is about 1.7 at birth and falls to about 1.0 by 8–10 years
A disproportionately short lower segment suggests a skeletal or endocrine cause
Laron dwarfism: growth hormone is high but IGF-1 is low (GH insensitivity)
Chronic malnutrition stunts height-for-age over time
Height below the 3rd percentile or a falling growth velocity needs evaluation
Turner syndrome is a key cause of short stature in girls
topics.title: Growth & Short Stature
topics.trap: High GH with short stature is not GH excess — with low IGF-1 it is Laron dwarfism (GH receptor defect).

topics.oneLiner: Ventilate first; compressions below 60; term babies start on room air.
points: Preterm is born before 37 weeks; post-term at or after 42 weeks; low birth weight is below 2,500 g
Meconium normally passes within 24 hours (up to 48 hours in preterm babies)
Vitamin K is given at birth to prevent haemorrhagic disease of the newborn (VKDB)
Neonatal resuscitation starts with drying, warmth and airway positioning
Chest compressions begin when the heart rate remains below 60/min despite effective ventilation
A term newborn is resuscitated starting with room air (21% oxygen), not 100% oxygen
The spinal cord in an infant ends at a higher level than in adults (around L3 at birth)
Neonatal hypothyroidism screening sample: cord blood at birth or a heel-prick sample after 48–72 hours
Early neonatal sepsis organisms: group B Streptococcus, E. coli and Listeria
topics.title: Neonatology Essentials & Resuscitation
topics.trap: 100% oxygen for a term newborn is outdated — resuscitation begins with room air and titrates up.

topics.askedAs: jaundice type from stool and timing
topics.oneLiner: Jaundice in the first 24 hours is always pathological; conjugated jaundice with pale stools means biliary atresia until disproved.
points: Jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours of life is pathological — usually haemolysis
Physiological jaundice appears after 24 hours, peaks around day 3–5 and is unconjugated
Conjugated jaundice with dark urine and clay-coloured stools: biliary atresia — Kasai portoenterostomy works best early
Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency causes neonatal cholestasis; liver biopsy shows PAS-positive granules
Breast milk jaundice is prolonged unconjugated jaundice in an otherwise thriving baby
Untreated severe unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia damages basal ganglia — kernicterus
Infant of a diabetic mother risks hypoglycaemia (treat below threshold with feeds/IV glucose), macrosomia and respiratory distress
Galactosaemia: jaundice, hepatomegaly, cataracts (oil-drop) and reducing sugar in urine
topics.title: Neonatal Jaundice & Metabolic Problems
topics.trap: Any conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia in a newborn is abnormal — 'physiological' applies only to unconjugated jaundice.

topics.oneLiner: Sac present = omphalocele; no sac, bowel beside the cord = gastroschisis.
points: Tracheo-oesophageal fistula: frothy salivation, choking with feeds, nasogastric tube cannot be passed
Oesophageal atresia babies drool from birth; the commonest type has a distal fistula
Omphalocele: viscera herniate through the cord covered by a membranous sac; associated anomalies are common
Gastroschisis: bowel herniates beside the cord with no covering sac; fewer associated anomalies
Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (Bochdalek, posterolateral): scaphoid abdomen, bowel sounds in the chest
Choanal atresia: cyanosis that improves when the baby cries; a catheter cannot be passed through the nose
Congenital hypertrophic pyloric stenosis: projectile non-bilious vomiting at 3–6 weeks, palpable 'olive', hypochloraemic alkalosis
Hirschsprung disease: delayed meconium, explosive stool on rectal examination; rectal biopsy is the gold standard
Meningomyelocele: sac on the back containing cord tissue, linked to folate deficiency
topics.title: The Surgical Neonate
topics.trap: CHPS vomiting is non-bilious — bilious vomiting in a newborn is a surgical emergency of a different kind (malrotation).

topics.askedAs: deficiency from signs, SAM from MUAC
topics.oneLiner: Rosary and wide wrists are rickets; bleeding gums are scurvy; perioral rash with diarrhoea is zinc.
points: SAM: MUAC below 11.5 cm, weight-for-height below −3 SD, or bilateral pitting oedema
A child with MUAC 10.5 cm but a good appetite has uncomplicated SAM — community-based treatment
Shock in SAM: cautious IV fluids (e.g. Ringer lactate with glucose) — the SAM heart tolerates overload poorly
Vitamin A prophylaxis: 1,00,000 IU at 9 months, then 2,00,000 IU every 6 months up to 5 years
Vitamin A treatment of deficiency/measles: age-based dose on days 1, 2 and 14 (1,00,000 IU under 1 year; 2,00,000 IU above)
Rickets: craniotabes, rachitic rosary, Harrison sulcus, widened wrists, bowed legs
Scurvy (Barlow disease): bleeding swollen gums, petechiae, painful limbs, poor wound healing
Acrodermatitis enteropathica: perioral and perianal rash with diarrhoea — zinc deficiency
Iron deficiency in toddlers shows with pica (eating chalk, soil) and microcytic anaemia
topics.title: Nutrition, SAM & Vitamin Deficiencies
topics.trap: The vitamin A dose halves below 1 year of age — 1,00,000 IU, not 2,00,000 IU.

topics.askedAs: IMNCI class and plan from signs
topics.oneLiner: Eager to drink with a slow skin pinch is some dehydration: Plan B, 75 mL/kg ORS over 4 hours.
points: Some dehydration: restless/irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, skin pinch returns slowly
Severe dehydration: lethargic, very sunken eyes, drinks poorly or not at all, pinch returns in over 2 seconds
Plan B (some dehydration): ORS 75 mL/kg over 4 hours, then reassess
Plan C (severe dehydration): rapid IV fluids — 100 mL/kg Ringer lactate in divided aliquots by age
Zinc is given with ORS for 14 days in childhood diarrhoea
Fast breathing cut-offs: ≥60/min under 2 months, ≥50/min at 2–12 months, ≥40/min at 1–5 years
A 3-month-old with fast breathing alone (no indrawing, no danger signs) has IMNCI pneumonia, not severe disease
General danger signs: unable to drink, vomits everything, convulsions, lethargic or unconscious
Diarrhoea lasting 14 days or more is persistent diarrhoea
topics.title: Diarrhoea, Dehydration & IMNCI
topics.trap: Plan B is 75 mL/kg over 4 hours — the exam's '3-hour' phrasing still expects the standard Plan B volume.

topics.askedAs: organism or feature that names the disease
topics.oneLiner: Koplik spots before the rash mean measles; a membrane that bleeds means diphtheria.
points: Measles: fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, Koplik spots, then a rash starting behind the ears
Vitamin A is part of measles management and prevents eye damage
Diphtheria: grey pseudomembrane that bleeds on removal, bull neck; treatment is antitoxin plus antibiotics
Mumps: parotitis with orchitis in post-pubertal boys
Hand-foot-mouth disease: vesicles on palms, soles and mouth — Coxsackie A16
Commonest cause of bacterial meningitis in a 1-year-old: Streptococcus pneumoniae
Simple febrile seizures occur at 6 months–5 years; first-line treatment of a prolonged seizure is a benzodiazepine
Kawasaki disease with coronary aneurysms: IV immunoglobulin plus aspirin
Acute rheumatic fever follows streptococcal sore throat — Jones criteria, raised ASO titre
topics.title: Childhood Infections & Emergencies
topics.trap: Diphtheria's membrane bleeds when scraped off — that single detail separates it from candidiasis and tonsillitis in stems.

topics.askedAs: murmur or X-ray that names the lesion
topics.oneLiner: Fixed split S2 is ASD; boot-shaped heart with cyanotic spells is tetralogy of Fallot.
points: VSD is the commonest congenital heart disease overall
ASD: widely split second heart sound that is fixed — it does not vary with respiration
Tetralogy of Fallot: VSD, overriding aorta, pulmonary stenosis, right ventricular hypertrophy
Cyanotic spells in TOF are relieved by squatting (raises systemic resistance)
TOF chest X-ray: boot-shaped heart with a concave pulmonary bay
Croup (laryngotracheitis): barking cough, stridor, steeple sign on neck X-ray
Epiglottitis: drooling, thumbprint sign — do not depress the tongue to look
Foreign body inhalation: rigid bronchoscopy is the procedure of choice
Cystic fibrosis: recurrent chest infections, thick sputum, malabsorption; sweat chloride is the gold standard
topics.title: Heart & Airway Favourites
topics.trap: A split S2 that varies with breathing is normal; ASD's split is fixed — that word decides the answer.

topics.askedAs: syndrome from urine or blood findings
topics.oneLiner: Normal light microscopy with foot-process effacement on EM is minimal change disease.
points: Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, oedema, hypoalbuminaemia, hyperlipidaemia
Minimal change disease is the commonest cause of nephrotic syndrome in children
Electron microscopy in minimal change disease shows effacement of podocyte foot processes
First-line treatment of childhood nephrotic syndrome: oral prednisolone
RBC casts in urine mean glomerular bleeding — think post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis
Haemophilia A: prolonged aPTT, normal PT and platelet count, haemarthroses in boys
Iron is the antidote-relevant poison: deferoxamine chelates iron in iron tablet poisoning
Thalassaemia major: transfusion-dependent microcytic anaemia; HPLC/Hb electrophoresis confirms
Lead poisoning: abdominal pain, developmental delay, blue gum line, basophilic stippling
topics.title: Kidney, Blood & Poisoning
topics.trap: Haemophilia prolongs aPTT only — a normal PT and platelet count in a bleeding boy points straight to factor deficiency.

topics.askedAs: tumour from site, age and behaviour
topics.oneLiner: A flank mass that does not cross the midline is Wilms; the one that crosses and calcifies is neuroblastoma.
points: Wilms tumour (nephroblastoma): painless abdominal mass in a 2–5-year-old, usually does not cross the midline
Neuroblastoma: commonest extracranial solid tumour of childhood; arises from adrenal/sympathetic tissue
Neuroblastoma metastasises early, can cross the midline, and may cause opsoclonus-myoclonus
ALL is the commonest leukaemia of childhood
Burkitt lymphoma: fast-growing jaw mass in children, starry-sky histology, linked to EBV
Perthes disease: avascular necrosis of the femoral head — hip pain and limp at 4–8 years, internal rotation lost first
Osteogenesis imperfecta: recurrent fractures, blue sclera, dentinogenesis imperfecta, family history
A painless jaw swelling with starry-sky biopsy in a child is Burkitt until disproved
topics.title: Childhood Tumours & Orthopaedic Favourites
topics.trap: Multiple fractures at different healing stages in an infant suggest osteogenesis imperfecta (or abuse) — not rickets alone.

topics.oneLiner: 21 Down, 5p cri-du-chat, paternal 15q Prader-Willi, maternal inheritance for mitochondria.
points: Down syndrome (trisomy 21): hypotonia, flat facies, upslanting palpebral fissures, single palmar crease
Down syndrome associations: duodenal atresia, Hirschsprung disease, hypothyroidism, leukaemia risk
Cri-du-chat syndrome: deletion of 5p — microcephaly and a high-pitched cat-like cry
Prader-Willi syndrome: deletion of paternal chromosome 15q11–13 — hypotonia, then hyperphagia and obesity
Angelman syndrome is the maternal 15q deletion counterpart (imprinting)
Klinefelter (47,XXY): tall boy, small testes, gynaecomastia, infertility
Mitochondrial disorders are inherited only from the mother
Congenital toxoplasmosis triad: chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, intracranial calcifications
Bruton agammaglobulinaemia: absent B cells and all immunoglobulins low — recurrent bacterial infections after 6 months
topics.title: Genetics & Classic Syndromes
topics.trap: Prader-Willi is the paternal deletion; the same region deleted from the mother gives Angelman.
